newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo "disappointed" at CVRD bid failure.
newsitem.headline: Anglo "disappointed" at CVRD bid failure.

text.p: Anglo American Corporation of South Africa Ltd said on Wednesday it was disappointed at its failure to buy the controlling stake in Brazilian state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) as part of a consortium.
"Naturally, we are disappointed because I think it is clear that we devoted considerable attention to this over the past few months," Anglo director Michael Spicer told Reuters.
A consortium led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN paid 3.338 billion reais ($3.15 billion) for a 41.73 percent voting stake in CVRD.
At 32 reais a share, the government received a 19.98 percent premium on the 26.67 reais per share minimum price.
Spicer said Anglo was not prepared to overpay, especially if there was little chance of recovering value from CVRD in the near future.
"However, part of that attention was an extremely thorough due diligence of CVRD and we always felt that the minimum price when it was set, was pretty full.
"So we had set clear parameters as to what levels represented value and we weren't prepared to overpay, let alone significantly overpay.

"In a bidding situation like that, you can always stretch a little bit but if you get into uncharted territory and there is no chance of recovering value in the foreseeable future then clearly one has got to decide to pull out," Spicer said.
The winning Valepar consortium still has the option to raise its controlling stake to 45 percent of voting shares.
In addition to CSN, the consortium consists of NationsBank Corp, Banco Safra, investment fund Opportunity Asset Management, and four Brazilian pension funds.
Paper and pulp firm Cia Suzano de Papel and Celulose was in the group while another South African mining company, Gencor Ltd, has signed a letter of intent to join if they won.
Spicer said although Anglo was not part of the winning consortium, the company and its offshore arm Minorco still remained committed to Brazil.
"Anglo and Minorco are long-term Brazilian players, we have a two-decade track record there".
He said Anglo had a number of other opportunities in Brazil, including the Salobo project which is a joint venture between Minorco and CVRD.
A feasibility study into the project was completed in 1995 and an investment of $1.5 billion was needed to bring the project into production by the end of the century.

The study indicated that annual production from the Salabo resource, in the Carajas region of Para state, could be 200,000 tonnes of refined copper, 250,000 ounces of gold, together with silver and sulphuric acid.
